_provenance.rules: Plain English, no praise words, figures only where a listed source publishes them, never 'official boundary' (spec §18). Exactly one key fact 'Established YYYY (27 CFR 9.N)', as TTB lists it. Descriptions of 2-4 sentences, at most 700 characters. At most 8 grapes; the 1-3 signature grapes are PRINCIPAL and the rest ACCESSORY. At least two sources per place, one of them the CFR section or the Federal Register final rule. share_pct is left out.

article.description: A high-desert valley of about 665 square miles in Los Angeles and Kern counties, north of the San Gabriel Mountains, with a floor at 2,300 to 3,100 feet walled by mountains on three sides. Vines were planted here in the 1880s and 1890s; modern planting began in 1981, and by 2007 there were about 128 acres in 16 vineyards.
article.climate: Hot, dry summers and cold winters, Winkler Region V at about 4,600 growing degree days, with only 4 to 9 inches of rain and winter lows of 6 to 11 °F.
article.soils: Deep, loamy, well-drained alluvial soils from granite, such as the Hesperia-Rosamond-Cajon and Hanford-Ramona-Greenfield associations.
article.grape_varieties: Cabernet Sauvignon, Tempranillo and Malbec, with Muscat, on the estates of the valley.
article.wine_styles: Dry red wines from Cabernet Sauvignon, Tempranillo and Malbec.

article.description: A basin of about 150,400 acres in southwestern Monterey County, the watershed of the San Antonio River, encircled by the Santa Lucia Range between the Pacific and the Salinas Valley. article.soils: Around 40 soil series, mostly alluvial on flat to gentle slopes, including Arbuckle gravelly loam, Lockwood loam and Placentia sandy loam.
article.grape_varieties: Cabernet Sauvignon, Petite Sirah and Syrah, with Grenache, Tempranillo and Marsanne among some 20 varieties.
article.wine_styles: Dry red wines from Cabernet Sauvignon, Petite Sirah and Rhône varieties.

article.climate: Moderate, with a maritime influence from Monterey Bay, about 20 miles away, and afternoon breezes; the mountain ranges shelter the valleys.
article.soils: Varied, because of seismic activity: soils shift from granite to limestone within feet, with ancient seabed deposits.
article.grape_varieties: Pinot Noir and Chardonnay make up more than half the county's vineyard; Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot and Zinfandel grow in the warmer spots.
article.wine_styles: Dry Chardonnay and Pinot Noir, and red wines from older Zinfandel plantings.

article.soils: Poorly drained clay and clay loam soils of the Delta's alluvial fans, basins and flood plains, from about 10 feet below to 5 feet above sea level.
article.grape_varieties: Chenin Blanc stands out, with Petite Sirah, Chardonnay and Pinot Gris.
article.wine_styles: Dry and off-dry Chenin Blanc, and red wines from Petite Sirah.

article.description: A coastal AVA of about 15,900 acres on the Palos Verdes Peninsula in southwestern Los Angeles County, a low mountain between the Los Angeles Plain and the Pacific, from sea level to about 1,460 feet at San Pedro Hill. Only about 7 acres of vines were planted at establishment.

article.grape_varieties: Pinot Noir, Chardonnay, Merlot and Cabernet Sauvignon, the varieties the final rule names.

article.climate: Hot summers and mild winters in a cool mountain valley, where rock tailings left by gold mining store the day's heat and help against frost.

article.grape_varieties: Riesling was the grape grown on the valley's only vineyard.

article.grape_varieties: Cabernet Sauvignon, Syrah and Tempranillo, with Sangiovese, Petite Sirah and Viognier.
article.wine_styles: Dry red wines from Bordeaux, Rhône, Spanish and Italian varieties.
